chunks: For what you have brought upon yourselves. God is surely not unjust to His creatures.

key_terms.بِمَا قَدَّمَتْ أَيْدِيكُمْ: By what your hands have sent before (your deeds)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean that God is not unjust to His servants in the context of divine retribution?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse from Surah Al-Anfal (8:51) is often cited to illustrate the principle of 'self-inflicted retribution,' where divine justice is not an arbitrary punishment but a direct consequence of human agency. It reinforces the concept that God’s fairness is absolute, and any hardship befalling a community is the tangible result of their own prior actions, distinguishing divine justice from divine injustice.
